Are they his dad's medals?  In which case, well, one COULD say stolen valor...but in a very stupid way.

But only a total douchebag would voluntarily wear their NDSM as a civilian.  I mean, it's absolutely hilarious.

Like, weapons-grade clown behavior.

The World War II Victory Medal was for anyone in the armed forces, 1941-1946.

Now, if Mr. Porter here had been 18 in 1946, he'd be 98 years old right now.

And, I don't think that guy is 98 years old.

So...what is he doing?!

I need you to understand what a joke of a medal this is among veterans.  Literally the definition of a participation trophy, except you don't have to even participate.

You could have spent your whole time during Vietnam drinking beer in Germany or spent Gulf War I in Lousiana.

You still get one.

The National Defense Service Medal means you were...alive and in the military during something the military thought was a conflict.

You didn't have to actually go there or have anything to do with it.

I got a NDSM while I was a West Point cadet because of...Gulf War I...in 1995. 

lmao

I need you people to understand what a total douchebag this guy is.  

Let's talk about the two ribbons he's wearing.

The World War II Victory Medal (top)
The National Defense Service Medal (bottom)
